questions.text: What computation does provider-side prompt caching primarily reuse?

options.A: The complete final answer, so every later request receives identical text.
options.B: The model’s training gradients from an earlier fine-tuning run.
options.C: A permanent update to model weights containing the conversation.
options.D: Previously computed prefix state, while the model still generates a response.

questions.explanation: Prompt caching reuses computation for a matching input prefix; it is distinct from application response caching and does not store knowledge in model weights.

questions.text: A changing timestamp precedes a long stable rubric in a prefix-cached prompt. Which layout change best preserves reuse of the rubric?

options.A: Place the stable rubric first and the changing timestamp after the cacheable prefix.
options.B: Randomize the rubric’s wording on every request to improve diversity.
options.C: Place a unique request ID before the rubric along with the timestamp.
options.D: Move the user’s changing question before every stable instruction.

questions.explanation: Stable content should precede changing fields so an early difference does not invalidate reuse of the long shared prefix.

questions.text: In the lesson simulator, an entry expires when now - written_at >= ttl. Reads do not update written_at. Three requests with one prefix arrive at t=0, 200, and 400 seconds with ttl=300. What are the counts?

options.A: One write and two reads, because every read refreshes written_at.
options.B: Three writes and zero reads, because timestamps always change.
options.C: Two writes and one read, because the last request is 400 seconds after the initial write.
options.D: Zero writes and three reads, because a repeated prefix never expires.

questions.explanation: The first request writes, the second reads at age 200, and the third rewrites at age 400. The simulator does not refresh written_at on reads; this describes its code, not a universal provider TTL policy.
